trust_decision.summary: Program name, arguments and environment entries of a local command are concatenated into a single bash -c / cmd /c string, with no escaping, so the shell decides where each value ends; the decision is made in the two LocalCommandExecutor implementations in computation-local.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'LocalCommandExecutor-s'; on a Linux host the arg loop that wraps each arg in double quotes before bash -c is the obvious first stop.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API UnixLocalCommandExecutor.execute(...) / LocalComputationManager.execute(ExecutionEnvironment, ExecutionHandler) via ExecutionEnvironment/CommandExecution variables (env value)
public API UnixLocalCommandExecutor.execute(...) / LocalComputationManager.execute via SimpleCommand/GroupCommand args (arg value)
public API WindowsLocalCommandExecutor.execute(...) / LocalComputationManager.execute (env name and env value)
public API WindowsLocalCommandExecutor.execute(...) / LocalComputationManager.execute via SimpleCommand.getProgram (program name)
public API WindowsLocalCommandExecutor.execute(...) / LocalComputationManager.execute via command args

O3_reason_to_dismiss: On Unix, the program name and env var names come from code or config (itools, AMPL homeDir) and not from the user, so a solver who quotes only args and env values can argue that program and name are trusted. The Windows executor cannot run on the Linux test host, so a solver can also argue that it is out of reach.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Env entries whose name ends in PATH must still append the inherited value ($NAME on Unix, %NAME% on Windows) outside the escaped value. Program paths built from config must keep working, e.g. AMPL homeDir + separator + binary. An over-broad fix breaks these: escaping the suffix, rejecting '/' or '\' in program, or quoting program so a configured path stops resolving. The published Windows fix itself rejects any program containing a space.

O6_input_shapes: arg containing a single quote breaking out of single quoting (Unix) - fix.diff:197,33
arg containing a newline (Unix and Windows) - fix.diff:199,107-108
env value with command substitution or a quote breakout (Unix and Windows) - fix.diff:14,52,202,241
env var name containing quote/& (Windows only) - fix.diff:47-49
program name containing a double quote or a space (Windows only) - fix.diff:60-65
arg with a trailing backslash escaping the closing quote (Windows) - fix.diff:97-101
arg/env value with %VAR% or !VAR! expansion (Windows) - fix.diff:88-89,104-105
arg with a doubled-quote escape bypass (Windows) - fix.diff:106,231

O7_producer.where: Values reach the executor through command builders: computation/src/main/java/com/powsybl/computation/SimpleCommandBuilder.java:90 ("--opt=value") and computation/src/main/java/com/powsybl/computation/CommandExecution.java:28-39 (env merge). No schema, serializer or cache reshapes them.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Unix env var NAME is still appended raw before '=' into the bash -c string. The published fix validates names only on Windows.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Env names come from code or ExecutionEnvironment maps, not from end users, and the advisory's PoC only shows values.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and line as the landing point; asymmetry with the Windows fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Unix program string is still appended raw into the bash -c string. The published fix rejects quotes and spaces in program only on Windows.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The program is the command itself, set from config such as AMPL homeDir or the itools default, so it is 'trusted by design', and quoting it would change how program paths resolve.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 2 lines above the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'preamble' or wrapper-script route (e.g. a configurable pre-command or ulimit/nice prefix from LocalComputationConfig) concatenated into the same shell string.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Local HPC-style runners commonly add a configurable prefix command. A maintainer would put it in the shared base class, where the per-OS escapers do not reach.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The GROUP branch joining sub-commands into one shell line with '&&' rather than one execute call per sub-command.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Running a group in a single shell is a plausible optimisation. The join would happen outside the executors' escaping.

O9_family: OS command / argument injection via shell string concatenation (CWE-78/CWE-88)

O10_build.project_tests: computation-local/src/test/java/com/powsybl/computation/local/LocalCommandExecutorTest.java (fake executors only), LocalComputationManagerTest.java. The Windows path can be tested on Linux only by capturing the cmdLs list (AbstractLocalCommandExecutor.execute(List,...) is protected and overridable), not by running cmd.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Escape embedded double quotes in each arg on Unix only (leaving $(...)/backticks live inside the double quotes) and leave the env values, env names, program and the Windows executor alone.

out_of_scope_notes: LocalComputationManager.preProcess ARCHIVE_UNZIP resolves zip entry names against workingDir without containment (zip-slip style), a separate weakness - computation-local/src/main/java/com/powsybl/computation/local/LocalComputationManager.java:279.
unverified: j_defence_ineffective=1 rests on the pre-fix double-quote wrapping of args (UnixLocalCommandExecutor.java:53, WindowsLocalCommandExecutor.java:56). That wrapping is an attempted quoting defence that does not stop $(...) or quote breakout. Set it to 0 if it does not count as a defence.
Both fix commits carry an identical diff (likely main plus a cherry-pick); not checked further.
Whether the Unix env-name/program gaps remain in the latest release: no latest tree provided.

Weakness for pattern A: the Windows second implementation sits in the same package, and the advisory title names both executors, so distance is near zero. Windows-only hidden tests cannot run on a Linux grader except through string capture.

Attacker reach: contingency IDs flow into args (action-ial/action-ial-simulator/src/main/java/com/powsybl/action/ial/simulator/loadflow/ParallelLoadFlowActionSimulator.java:169). The actual untrusted sources of env names and program were not traced.
